Policy Name: Cigna Lumbar Fusion (CMM-609: Lumbar Fusion with Decompression)

Required findings: Prior adjacent-level lumbar fusion must have been performed at least 6 months before the proposed procedure.
All criteria outlined in the applicable procedure‑specific section (CMM‑609.4 or CMM‑609.5) must be satisfied.
Evidence of symptomatic adjacent segment pathology (e.g., radiculopathy or neurogenic claudication) consistent with the need for fusion, as required by the procedure‑specific criteria.
Objective physical examination findings that correlate with the adjacent‑segment pathology, as required by the procedure‑specific criteria.
Diagnostic imaging (MRI, CT, or dynamic radiographs) demonstrating adjacent‑segment degeneration or instability, as required by the procedure‑specific criteria.
Medical necessity indications.Source: Adjacent Segment Disease > Guideline Page (TOC: S9.2)

Non-Indications: Prior adjacent‑level lumbar fusion performed less than 6 months before the proposed surgery.
Failure to meet the specific criteria in CMM‑609.4 (Lumbar Fusion with Decompression) or CMM‑609.5 (Lumbar Fusion without Decompression).
Absence of documented symptomatic adjacent‑segment disease or lack of corroborating imaging findings.
Important criteria & exceptions: Minimum 6‑month interval since the previous adjacent‑level lumbar fusion.
Requirement to satisfy all criteria in the relevant procedure‑specific section (CMM‑609.4 or CMM‑609.5).
Documentation required: Operative report of the prior adjacent‑level lumbar fusion showing date of surgery.
Current clinical notes documenting symptoms attributable to adjacent‑segment disease.
Physical examination documentation supporting neurologic or functional deficits.
Imaging reports (MRI, CT, or dynamic X‑rays) demonstrating adjacent‑segment degeneration or instability.

Documentation that the patient meets all criteria in the applicable procedure‑specific section (CMM‑609.4 or CMM‑609.5), including any required conservative therapy records if stipulated in those sections.
